Return the words to the situations in which people actually use them: asking, promising, calculating, grieving, playing. A philosophical knot may loosen when we see these differences clearly. Understanding can be a change of orientation in ordinary life, rather than another grand explanation.
What to recognize: Recognize language examined in its lived uses, or a philosophical confusion dissolved by exposing a misleading picture. This portrait emphasizes the later philosophy; it is not a summary of every period.

state.target_passage: Your site specification and the append-only, hash-chained schema are locked in, and I agree the Tucson-style thermal-inertia trap is exactly the kind of slow bias that makes cross-station comparison non-negotiable, so let's now pin down the calibration protocol that your "next-due calibration date" field in the instrument table actually activates. For temperature I'm specifying a two-point check: we ice-point (0 °C) and steam-point (100 °C at local barometric pressure, corrected) the aspirated sensor against a NIST-traceable platinum-resistance reference thermometer at installation, every two months in summer and every three months in winter, and we log both raw reference values and our computed offset into a dedicated calibration-event row in the instrument table so the known-offset field is never a single number but a sliding two-week median; for relative humidity we use two saturated-salt baths—sodium chloride at 75.3 % RH and magnesium chloride at 33.0 % RH at 20 °C—because they require no sealed chamber, just a jar and a lid with a wire seal, and we compare our capacitive probe's reading after it stabilizes (≥20 min in each bath), logging the deviation at each point rather than a single midpoint so we can see whether the sensor is drifting linearly or developing a curvature error; barometric pressure gets a weekly comparison against the NWS station's station-reduced value broadcast on the NOAA site (or, within 5 km, a hand-held aneroid with its own annual NIST certificate) and we accept the comparison only if wind is below 5 m/s and the mast reading is not in a pressure-spike (frontal passage), otherwise the row is quality-flagged 3 and excluded from the offset median; the two-component rain gauge—solid cylinder for liquid, separate tipping bucket for snow—gets a monthly weigh-and-measure audit where we dump the gauge contents into a pre-weighed beaker and verify the collected volume against the number of tips recorded by the datalogger, giving us an absolute volumetric check independent of the tipping mechanism itself. Now the failure I want us to design around specifically: tipping-bucket tip-weight corrosion. In a documented case from a suburban station in coastal Norfolk, Virginia, salt-air ingress into the bucket's pivot housing corroded the small aluminum tip weights over roughly two wet seasons, increasing the effective tipping mass from 0.200 mm-equivalent to about 0.230 mm-equivalent; during any single storm the deficit was roughly 2–3 mm out of a 40 mm event—well inside the station-to-station event scatter of ±5 mm—so the per-event quality flag never tripped, and the only signal was that the station's seasonal accumulated rainfall trailed the NWS station by about 45 mm after sixty-one recorded events, a gap that looked like ordinary orographic undercatch until someone overlayed the two season totals and noticed the discrepancy grew linearly with cumulative rainfall rather than remaining flat; in our protocol the monthly weigh-and-measure audit exists precisely to catch that drift within one or two events of onset, because the measured water volume in the cylinder will disagree with the datalogger's tip count by more than our accepted tolerance of ±2 mm per month, and when it does we open a mandatory recalibration ticket: the bucket is removed, tip weights are weighed against the factory spec on a 0.001 g balance, pivot clearance is inspected under a loupe for pitting, and the event is logged as a site-condition anomaly with a close-up photo of the corroded weights pinned to the instrument table so that the record itself documents the physical degradation rather than leaving a silent, unexplained seasonal deficit that a downstream climate analyst might attribute to a real wet-vs-dry year signal.
